rationale: The operator ordered capability EXPANSION with cua as the example. The cua runtime itself is not adoptable here (no docker/podman/qemu/gvisor/VMX — measured 01:26Z; their cloud fleet is tier C) — but their PATTERNS are exactly our culture formalized: probe-before-trust, permission-at-launch, action-ladder (GUI as last resort, evidence per action). Adopting the patterns on our NATIVE surfaces adds a real new hand — browser computer-use, proven live (example.com title read-back + 58,613B screenshot, 01:26:52Z) — without adding a single key, account, or chain. 'What can we do' becomes a judged book with receipts instead of tribal knowledge; the judge watches it on schedule so power can never silently rot into story.
risk: Low: the desk is keyless (ls-remote uses creds already embedded in the remotes; nothing printed, nothing stored), fail-soft exit 0, ABSENT is a legal verdict so CI runners without agent-browser stay green-honest (3 LIVE hands floor: shell+git+web). The browser probe touches only a public page (example.com) with no credentials and no writes. check #31 could false-RED if hands-book.json goes stale >25h — mitigated by wiring the desk into recruit.yml cadence alongside canon-liveness (same mitigation as Z-42's #30).
rollback: git revert the hands-book desk/book + audit-check hunk + eval hunk + registry row + recruit.yml step + docs edits. No books, signing lanes, or chain surfaces touched; /tmp screenshot probe artifacts are disposable.
